description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of error types observed in two models, labeled “Vanilla” and “HCL”. The chart is composed of five slices representing error categories: “Atomic Skill Fail”, “Correct”, “Reason Error”, “Question Misunderstood”, and an unnamed category. The “Vanilla” model data, shown on the left, consists of a dark teal slice labeled “Atomic Skill Fail” occupying approximately 68.0% of the pie, a light teal slice labeled “Correct” at 12.0%, a gray slice labeled “Reason Error” at 8.0%, and a dark gray slice labeled “Question Misunderstood” at 12.0%. The “HCL” model data, on the right, includes a dark teal slice representing “Atomic Skill Fail” at 55.0%, a light teal slice for “Correct” at 21.0%, a gray slice for “Reason Error” at 14.0%, and a dark gray slice for “Question Misunderstood” at 10.0%. Percentage labels are displayed inside each slice, and a legend identifying the colors and corresponding error types is provided above the chart. The slices are visually arranged in a clockwise order, and one slice from each chart is visually offset from the center.
